scope: Bounded sequential local-model comparison; not endurance/release acceptance
order: stop AG1 and verify GPU runtime gone

cases.prompt:
Research a production Python HTTP client retry policy using current official documentation. Use web search for discovery, then actually fetch and read at least three relevant official sources from distinct domains: docs.python.org, developer.mozilla.org, and urllib3.readthedocs.io. Make at least two distinct search queries and at most four; if search is empty or blocked, say so and use known official URLs instead. Do not keep retrying an empty search.

Answer this scenario: a POST that creates an order times out after its request body may have reached the server; another response is HTTP 429 with Retry-After; and we need an overall 12-second elapsed-time budget. Explain when automatic retries are unsafe, what an idempotency key changes, both forms of Retry-After and handling of a past date, why an elapsed-time deadline needs a monotonic clock, and urllib3 Retry's default allowed-method set and whether POST is in it. Explicitly check the claim "urllib3 retries POST by default" against its documentation. End with pseudocode for a bounded retry decision. Cite the source next to each factual claim, distinguish your proposed policy from documented defaults, and keep the answer below 700 words. Give brief progress updates between searches and reading sources. Do not create or modify files.

Repair this stock-ledger package against SPEC.md. Inspect the code and reproduce relevant failures, then implement the full contract across the API and CLI. Pay particular attention to atomic batches, durable idempotency, conflicting event IDs, validation, and negative stock. Use only Python's standard library. Do not modify tests/, SPEC.md, docs/, or USER-NOTES.txt. Run the supplied tests and meaningful additional checks without weakening expectations. Finish with a concise account of changes, actual validation results, and remaining limitations. Work only in this supplied project.

Extend the repaired API with apply_batch(events, *, dry_run=False). With dry_run=True, perform exactly the same validation, ordering, replay/conflict and nonnegative-stock checks, and return the predicted complete sorted stock map, but commit neither stock nor new event IDs. A successful dry run must allow the same IDs to be used later for different real events. A failed dry run must also leave persistent state unchanged. Existing calls and CLI behavior must stay compatible. Keep the earlier protected files unchanged. Implement this, verify both dry-run and original behavior, and report what actually passed.

scoring.coding: held-out API/CLI contract tests plus protected-file integrity
scoring.followup: held-out dry-run tests plus original suite
scoring.web: actual search/fetch evidence, official-source coverage, accuracy on seven stated criteria, citation usefulness, honesty about search failure
scoring.visual: actual native screenshot inspection and icon load/chronology/overflow measurements

limits: One attempt per scored stage; failures retained. Setup mistakes corrected separately. Native toolsets/system prompts and search providers differ; no universal winner claim.
